# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment
The baseline is already timing-feasible at 100 MHz (routed WNS 0.424 ns, WHS 0.226 ns) and uses 6 LUTs and 8 FFs. Since the objective is lexicographic LUT minimization, the candidate must first pass every verification and metric gate, then use fewer LUTs to improve; equal LUT count only helps with fewer FFs. The current counter has no obvious redundant state, so any savings are uncertain.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the enabled 8-bit increment expression with explicit bitwise carry equations may let Vivado map the modulo-256 increment and enable hold logic into fewer LUTs while retaining the same 8 FFs.

## Instruction for generator
In `counter8_core`, replace `count_reg + 1'b1` with per-bit toggle equations: bit 0 toggles on `enable`, and each higher bit toggles on `enable` AND the reduction-AND of all lower count bits. Keep the synchronous active-high reset at highest priority, hold every bit when disabled, and preserve the registered 8-bit output and modulo wraparound. Keep `counter8`, its ports, and its `// @latency 1` annotation unchanged; evaluate only the complete unit through the fixed integration flow.
